entries.summary: Grant access to this job.
details: Each entry needs a permission level and one identity. The current job template emits user_name and group_name permissions only. Service-principal entries remain in YAML but are not emitted. An explicit list replaces inherited permissions.

entries.summary: Choose the access level for this identity.
details: Select an access level supported for this resource, such as CAN_VIEW or CAN_MANAGE. Give the identity the access it needs to perform its role.

entries.summary: Identify a user by their email address.
details: Set only one of user_name, group_name and service_principal_name in an entry.

entries.summary: Grant this permission to a workspace group.
details: Use the group name, and leave user_name and service_principal_name unset in this entry.

entries.summary: Record a service-principal permission entry in the source YAML.
details: The current job template does not emit service-principal permissions. This entry is preserved for source compatibility; it does not grant access through generated job YAML.

entries.summary: Limit how many runs of this job execute at the same time.
details: Use queue.enabled to decide whether additional runs wait when this limit is reached. This is independent of pipeline streaming concurrency.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; LHP’s built-in limit is 1.

entries.summary: Control how runs wait for available job capacity.
details: Enable queue.enabled to let additional runs wait after maximum concurrent runs is reached.

entries.summary: Queue new runs while the concurrency limit is reached.
details: This controls waiting runs; max_concurrent_runs controls how many may execute simultaneously.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; LHP enables queuing by default.

entries.summary: Choose the performance target for job compute.
details: STANDARD is the built-in target. PERFORMANCE_OPTIMIZED favors faster compute startup at higher cost.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; LHP’s built-in target is STANDARD.

entries.summary: Limit the duration of a job run in seconds.
details: For example, 3600 is one hour. The timeout applies to the job rather than an individual data-quality check.
entries.unsetBehavior: Inherit project defaults; when no level sets it, LHP emits no timeout_seconds setting.

entries.summary: Add labels to the generated job resource.
details: Per-job tags merge with project defaults by key; values are rendered as quoted values. These are separate from Unity Catalog dataset tags.

entries.summary: Notify email recipients about job run events.
details: Configure separate recipient lists for start, success and failure. Per-event lists replace inherited lists.

entries.summary: Notify these addresses when a run starts.
details: This event’s recipient list replaces the inherited list; leaving it unset preserves inherited recipients.

entries.summary: Notify these addresses when a run succeeds.
details: This event’s recipient list replaces the inherited list; leaving it unset preserves inherited recipients.

entries.summary: Notify these addresses when a run fails.
details: This event’s recipient list replaces the inherited list; leaving it unset preserves inherited recipients.

entries.summary: Send job lifecycle events to configured notification destinations.
details: Entries reference destination IDs. Configure the destination separately, then reference its ID for the relevant event.

entries.summary: Run the job on a time-based schedule.
details: A schedule combines a Quartz cron expression, timezone and pause status. Check the timezone as well as the time before enabling it.

entries.summary: Define when the job runs using Quartz cron syntax.
details: Quartz includes seconds. The example runs daily at 08:00 in schedule.timezone_id; a five-field Unix cron expression is not equivalent.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
schedule:
  quartz_cron_expression: "0 0 8 * * ?"
  timezone_id: Australia/Melbourne
  pause_status: PAUSED

entries.summary: Choose the timezone used to interpret the schedule.
details: Use an IANA timezone such as Australia/Melbourne or UTC. This setting affects the scheduled time, not timestamps stored in your data.

entries.summary: Enable or pause scheduled runs without deleting the schedule.
details: PAUSED keeps the schedule configured while preventing its scheduled runs. UNPAUSED enables it.

choices.explanation: Keep the schedule without starting scheduled runs.

entries.summary: Configure an event-based job trigger.
details: Provide a supported trigger mapping, such as file_arrival or table_update. LHP passes this block into job YAML; use a scheduling approach supported by the job service.

entries.summary: Configure continuous job execution.
details: This is the job-level continuous block, not pipeline continuous mode. Use supported job settings such as pause_status.

entries.summary: Choose the identity that executes the job.
details: Set a supported run-as mapping such as service_principal_name. Job permissions separately control who may access or manage it.

entries.summary: Choose a remote Git source for job code.
details: Use the job service’s Git source fields, including URL/provider and the intended branch, tag or commit. This does not change your local LHP checkout.

entries.summary: Set job health rules evaluated by the job service.
details: LHP passes the health block through to generated job YAML. Health rules are distinct from data tests defined inside a flowgroup.

entries.summary: Generate a master job that chains orchestration jobs.
details: Only job_config project defaults control this setting. Per-job and monitoring-job values have no effect, and this key is not emitted into the job resource.
entries.unsetBehavior: LHP enables master-job generation by default.

entries.summary: Override the generated master orchestration job’s name.
details: Set this in job_config project defaults. Per-job and monitoring-job values are ignored.
entries.unsetBehavior: LHP derives the master-job name from the project.

entries.summary: Override compute for the monitoring union notebook task.
details: This block is used only by monitoring jobs. Use new_cluster for a cluster specification or existing_cluster_id for an existing cluster.

entries.summary: Define a cluster for the monitoring union notebook.
details: Fields inside this mapping, such as spark_version, node_type_id and num_workers, are rendered as written. A new_cluster mapping takes precedence over existing_cluster_id.

entries.summary: Use an existing cluster for the monitoring notebook.
details: Used only when notebook_cluster.new_cluster is absent. This setting applies to the monitoring union notebook, not orchestration pipeline tasks.
